sections.title: Technical SEO
sections.description: Crawlable, indexable, fast, and correctly structured.

items.title: Publish a valid robots.txt
items.why: Tells crawlers what to fetch or skip.
items.how: Serve /robots.txt at the root; allow public pages, disallow admin/cart/private paths; link the sitemap.

items.title: Generate and submit an XML sitemap
items.why: Helps engines discover pages faster.
items.how: Generate /sitemap.xml with lastmod; reference it in robots.txt; submit in Search Console + Bing.

items.title: Key pages return 200 and are indexable
items.why: A blocked or erroring page cannot rank.
items.how: Crawl the site; fix 4xx/5xx on canonical pages; verify no accidental noindex.

items.title: Self-referencing canonical tags
items.why: Prevents duplicate-content dilution.
items.how: Each indexable page has <link rel=canonical> to itself; paginate with proper canonicals.

items.title: Audit noindex/nofollow
items.why: Accidental noindex de-lists pages.
items.how: Grep templates for noindex; confirm only private/thin pages are excluded.

items.title: Serve everything over HTTPS
items.why: A ranking signal and a trust requirement.
items.how: Force HTTPS, redirect http→https with a single 301, fix mixed content.

items.title: Use 301s for moved URLs; no chains
items.why: Preserves equity and avoids loops.
items.how: Map old→new with a single hop; avoid chains and redirect loops.

items.title: Consistent trailing slash + case
items.why: Duplicate URLs split signals.
items.how: Pick one canonical form; redirect the other; lowercase paths.

items.title: Mobile-first responsive design
items.why: Google indexes the mobile version.
items.how: Responsive layout, tappable targets, no horizontal scroll.

items.title: Server-render or prerender JS content
items.why: Crawlers may not execute heavy client JS.
items.how: Use SSR/SSG or prerender; ensure primary content is in the HTML.

items.title: hreflang for multi-language sites
items.why: Serves the right locale and avoids duplicates.
items.how: Add reciprocal hreflang tags per locale; include x-default.

items.title: JSON-LD structured data on key page types
items.why: Rich results + machine-readable facts for AI.
items.how: Organization, WebSite, BreadcrumbList, Article/Product, FAQPage, HowTo, LocalBusiness as relevant.

items.title: Open Graph + Twitter card tags
items.why: Better sharing and click-through.
items.how: og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url, twitter:card.

items.title: Core Web Vitals in the good range
items.why: A ranking signal and a real UX win.
items.how: LCP ≤2.5s, INP ≤200ms, CLS ≤0.1 at p75; optimize images, JS, fonts, server.

items.title: Descriptive alt text + modern image formats
items.why: Image search + accessibility + speed.
items.how: Alt on every image, AVIF/WebP, width/height set, lazy-load below the fold.

items.title: Real 404s (no soft-404s)
items.why: Soft-404s waste crawl budget and confuse users.
items.how: Return HTTP 404 for missing pages; a helpful 404 page is fine.

items.title: Unique, keyword-relevant title tags
items.why: A primary ranking + CTR lever.
items.how: One <title> per page, 50–60 chars, primary keyword near the front, brand at the end.

items.title: Compelling meta descriptions
items.why: Improves click-through from search.
items.how: 150–160 chars, includes the value + a soft CTA; unique per page.

items.title: One H1 + logical H2/H3 structure
items.why: Clarifies topic and structure.
items.how: Single H1; section headings as H2; no heading levels skipped.

items.title: Map keywords to search intent
items.why: Matching intent is how you rank.
items.how: One primary intent per page; cover related questions; avoid cannibalisation.

items.title: Answer the question completely
items.why: Thin content doesn't rank and AI won't cite it.
items.how: Cover the topic, examples, and edge cases; be specific and original.

items.title: E-E-A-T signals
items.why: Trust is a ranking factor, especially for YMYL.
items.how: Author bios, About/Contact, credentials, sources, clear ownership.

items.title: FAQ section with FAQPage schema
items.why: Wins rich results and gives AI quotable answers.
items.how: Real questions users ask; concise answers; matching JSON-LD FAQPage.

items.title: Keep key content fresh
items.why: Recency matters for many queries.
items.how: Update dates and facts; show a visible updated date; refresh thin pages.

items.title: Breadcrumb navigation + BreadcrumbList
items.why: Improves UX and shows hierarchy to engines.
items.how: Visible breadcrumbs + matching JSON-LD.

items.title: Descriptive internal links
items.why: Spreads authority and helps discovery.
items.how: Link related pages with descriptive anchors; no 'click here'.

items.title: Remove or improve thin/duplicate pages
items.why: Thin pages dilute the site.
items.how: Merge duplicates, add value, or noindex low-value pages.

sections.title: AI Discovery (AEO / GEO)
sections.description: Be crawlable, machine-readable, and quotable by AI answer engines.

items.title: Allow AI search/retrieval crawlers
items.why: These produce AI citations (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot).
items.how: In robots.txt, allow OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot (and Googlebot/Bingbot).

items.title: Decide your AI training-crawler policy
items.why: Training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot) are a business choice.
items.how: Allow or block them explicitly in robots.txt; document the decision.

items.title: Publish /llms.txt (and /llms-full.txt)
items.why: A machine-readable index for LLMs — cheap, but not yet universally read.
items.how: List your key pages with short descriptions; don't rely on it alone.

items.title: Clear entity + brand facts in structured data
items.why: AI needs to know who you are.
items.how: Organization/WebSite JSON-LD with name, url, logo, sameAs (social), contact.

items.title: Write concise, quotable answers
items.why: AI cites explicit, verifiable statements.
items.how: Lead with the answer, then detail; use definitions, lists, dates, and sources.

items.title: Q&A / HowTo content + schema
items.why: Matches conversational queries.
items.how: FAQPage / HowTo JSON-LD; short direct answers.

items.title: ChatGPT Apps / MCP (if you have an app or action)
items.why: The path to the ChatGPT app directory.
items.how: Build an MCP server with the Apps SDK, then submit via the plugin portal.

items.title: List on AI directories / MCP registries
items.why: Discovery happens in directories too.
items.how: Submit to MCP directories and relevant AI tool lists.

sections.title: Submissions & Verification
sections.description: Where to submit your site/platform. Do these once, then verify.

items.title: Google Search Console
items.why: The source of truth for Google indexing + performance.
items.how: Add the property (Domain or URL prefix), verify via DNS or HTML, submit the sitemap, check Coverage/Pages.

items.title: Bing Webmaster Tools
items.why: Bing powers Bing + Copilot search.
items.how: Add the site, verify, submit the sitemap, review Index/Performance.

items.title: IndexNow (instant indexing)
items.why: Pushes new/updated URLs to Bing/Yandex instantly.
items.how: Generate a key, host /<key>.txt, POST URL updates to the IndexNow endpoint.

items.title: Google Business Profile (local)
items.why: Local pack visibility for physical/service businesses.
items.how: Create/claim the profile, verify, add hours, photos, categories, reviews.

items.title: Submit a ChatGPT App (if applicable)
items.why: Appears in the ChatGPT app directory.
items.how: Build with the Apps SDK (MCP server, OAuth, domain verification), meet the app guidelines, submit via the plugin submission portal, pass review.

items.title: MCP directory / registry
items.why: Discovery for AI clients that use MCP.
items.how: Publish your MCP server metadata and link it from your docs; list in MCP registries.

items.title: Apple App Store / Google Play (if mobile)
items.why: Where mobile users find you.
items.how: Complete store listing, screenshots, keywords; follow store review policies.

sections.title: Measurement (before / after)
sections.description: Prove the improvement with real data.

items.title: Capture a GSC baseline
items.why: You can't show before/after without a before.
items.how: Performance → export clicks, impressions, CTR, average position (28 days); store it.

items.title: Track clicks/impressions/CTR/position
items.why: Directional proof of ranking movement.
items.how: Compare snapshots with examples/ranking.mjs; watch trends, not single days.

items.title: Core Web Vitals field data
items.why: Confirms real-user speed, not just lab.
items.how: Check the CWV report in GSC / CrUX after shipping speed fixes.

items.title: Monitor AI citations
items.why: AEO success is being cited, not just crawled.
items.how: Periodically ask ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini your key questions; note brand mentions/citations.

items.title: Re-measure after improvements
items.why: Closes the loop; proves impact.
items.how: Wait for recrawl (days), export the same GSC metrics, compare with ranking.mjs, show the chart.
